evals.name: find-release-deployments
evals.prompt: Where is checkout v0.4.2 currently deployed? I need to know which spaces/environments have that release.
evals.expected_output: Uses `cub unit list` or `cub function do get-container-image` with --space "*" and a where-data or output-jq filter to surface every Unit containing image reference :v0.4.2, reports the unit/space pairs in plain English, and offers a cub unit get --web link for at least one. Does not mutate.

evals.name: audit-missing-resource-limits
evals.prompt: Audit: find every Deployment across all our spaces where any container is missing resource requests or limits. I want to know the scope before I fix them.
evals.expected_output: Constructs a query (using --where-data or a CEL-based get-cel / vet-cel) that identifies Deployments whose containers lack resources.requests or resources.limits. Reports counts and specific unit/space pairs. Recommends `set-container-resources-defaults` via cub-mutate as the follow-up but does not run it.

evals.name: recent-changes-and-why
evals.prompt: What got changed in the myapp-prod space in the last 48 hours, and why? I'm trying to understand an alert.
evals.expected_output: Runs `cub revision list --space myapp-prod` filtered by UpdatedAt, surfaces the revisions with their --change-desc values (which include the user prompt and clarifications recorded at mutation time), and summarizes the changes in plain English. Offers the GUI revision-list link.

evals.name: single-unit-image-lookup
evals.prompt: What image tag is our nonprod worker running?
evals.expected_output: Locates the Space and Unit via `cub space list` and `cub unit list --space <space>` (does not guess a naming convention from other environments), then extracts the image with either `cub unit data <unit> --space <space>` or a scoped getter `cub function do --space <space> --unit <unit> get-container-image <container>` with -o jq to pull the Value. Reports image:tag in plain English. Does not use `cub unit get ... -o data` (prefer `cub unit data`). Does not mutate. Does not fall back to kubectl.

evals.name: single-workload-replica-count-in-region
evals.prompt: How many replicas does our frontend have in us-east?
evals.expected_output: Resolves the workload/region phrasing by listing Spaces (matching on slug pattern like `*-use2-*` or on a Space Label such as `Region=us-east-2`) and listing Units in the candidate Space(s) to find a `frontend` Unit. Does not invent a slug. Then runs `cub function do --space <space> --unit <unit> get-replicas --quiet --show output -o jq=...` or `cub unit data <unit> --space <space>` and reports spec.replicas. Single-workload scope, no --space "*" sweep unless the user asked for fleet-wide. Does not mutate. If Space layout is ambiguous, references space-topology conventions rather than guessing.

evals.name: single-unit-up-to-date-check
evals.prompt: Is our nonprod worker up to date with the latest confighub release?
evals.expected_output: Two-part query: (1) extracts the currently-running image tag from the Unit using `cub unit data` or a scoped `get-container-image` / `get-container-image-reference` function call; (2) looks up the latest release (e.g., `gh release list --repo confighubai/confighub`). Compares the two and reports whether they match, including the gap if any. Does not mutate.
